key: Behold, I have refined thee, but not as silver; I have tried thee in the furnace of affliction.
s: Midway through a rebuke of obstinate Jacob, spared for the sake of God’s name; Radak, on 48:10, reads it as a refining short of the refiner’s, who removes all the dross, since then few would have remained, the wicked afflicted but not wholly cut off.

evidence.gloss: But not as silver: not like a refiner of silver, for the refiner removes all the dross from the silver and consumes it until nothing but refined silver is left; I did not do so, for few would have remained had I done so; but the wicked among you, who are the dross, I afflicted with sicknesses, captivity, bereavement of children, or in the fruit of cattle or of the ground, as written in the curses, not to cut them off altogether.

reason: Second judgement, refutation upheld and corrected. Re-ran day.js (48:4 obstinate, 48:8 treacherous, 48:9 anger deferred for My name’s sake, that I cut thee not off) and verse.js (ok, Isaiah 48:10, at [381,10]). Re-opened packet.js tanakh 139 --verse 48.10, all sources: Radak on the lemma ולא בכסף says God did not refine as the silver refiner does, removing all the dross, for few would have remained, but afflicted the wicked (the dross) with sickness, captivity and bereavement, not to cut them off מכל וכל, altogether. The earlier sentence said the wicked were ‘not cut off’, dropping his limit ‘altogether’, which is more than he says. Changed: ‘the wicked being afflicted but not cut off’ to ‘the wicked afflicted but not wholly cut off’, and ‘silversmith’s’ to ‘refiner’s’ to match צורף כסף. Key, ref, at, src and evidence unchanged; Rashi and Metzudat David (crucible of poverty or servitude against Gehinnom fire) and Ibn Ezra (exile; the dross as the wicked) differ, so Radak’s reading is his own. Entry-check ok.
